passage.title: Alcance de los documentos del restaurante
target: Julián Ibarra es contador independiente y atiende a restaurantes pequeños.
Dueño: Tengo muchos papeles, pero no sé cuál es la prioridad para este mes.
Julián: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos bancarios de los últimos seis meses.
Dueño: ¿Y los informes de ventas también?
Julián: Sí, y solo las facturas de proveedores de este año; el registro de nómina lo vemos después.
Dueño: Entonces empecemos por los extractos.
Julián: Confirmo el alcance por escrito, y revisaré la documentación antes del viernes.
native: Julián Ibarra is an independent accountant who serves small restaurants.
Owner: I have many papers, but I do not know which is the priority for this month.
Julián: We need you to send us the bank statements from the last six months.
Owner: And the sales reports too?
Julián: Yes, and only this year's supplier invoices; we will look at the payroll record later.
Owner: Then let us start with the statements.
Julián: I will confirm the scope in writing, and I will review the documentation before Friday.

words.note: Any written or digital entry of a transaction or document.
The complete set of records for a task or a client.
The item that needs attention first.
The defined limits of the work to be done.
Account summary from the bank for a period.
A summary of sales for a period.
A business that sells goods or services to the client.
A written agreement between two parties.
The system and list of wages paid to employees. Planilla is used in some Latin American countries.
An independent review of records and statements.

words.es: Necesitamos que nos envíe los extractos bancarios.
words.en: We need you to send us the bank statements.

words.es: ¿Cuál es la prioridad para este mes?
words.en: What is the priority for this month?

words.es: Empecemos por los extractos de los últimos seis meses.
words.en: Let's start with the bank statements from the last six months.

words.es: Solo necesitamos los documentos del año fiscal.
words.en: We only need the documents for the tax year.

words.es: Confirmo el alcance del servicio por escrito.
words.en: I confirm the scope of the service in writing.

example.target: Necesito los extractos del último trimestre.
example.native: I need the statements from the last quarter.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. After necesitar, use que plus the subjunctive when the action belongs to another person: necesitamos que envíe.

example.target: Le envío el alcance por escrito.
example.native: I will send you the scope in writing.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb with the stress accent on envío and envían. The indirect pronoun le names the recipient of what is sent.

example.target: Revisamos la documentación antes del cierre.
example.native: We review the documentation before the close.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In a future plan, use the future tense for a definite promise: revisaré.

example.target: Le pido que envíe el registro de nómina.
example.native: I ask you to send the payroll record.

verbs.note: Pedir takes que plus the subjunctive when a specific action is requested. Stem change e to i in the singular and ellos forms.

passage.title: Un horno nuevo en la cocina
target: Teresa revisa la compra del horno con el dueño del restaurante.
Dueño: Compré el horno para la cocina principal y pagué 4.500 euros por él.
Teresa: ¿Para qué es la compra, para reemplazar uno viejo o para una ampliación?
Dueño: Para reemplazar el anterior, que ya estaba roto.
Teresa: Entonces no es una reparación, sino un activo fijo que se deprecia.
Dueño: ¿Y el arreglo de la campana de extracción?
Teresa: Ese es un gasto de mantenimiento; lo registro en la cuenta de gastos del mes.
native: Teresa reviews the oven purchase with the restaurant owner.
Owner: I bought the oven for the main kitchen and paid 4,500 euros for it.
Teresa: What is the purchase for, to replace an old one or for an expansion?
Owner: To replace the previous one, which was already broken.
Teresa: Then it is not a repair, but a fixed asset that depreciates.
Owner: And the repair of the extractor hood?
Teresa: That is a maintenance expense; I record it in the expense account for the month.

words.note: The category given to a transaction in the accounts.
A long-lasting item used in the business, such as an oven.
A cost to keep an existing asset working.
An item or service bought by the business.
The account in which an expense is recorded.
The gradual reduction in an asset's recorded value over time.
Work that restores an item to working condition.
A plan of expected revenue and costs. It also means a written quote from a supplier.
The reason a purchase is made.
A document that proves a transaction, such as a receipt or invoice.

words.es: El horno es para la cocina principal.
words.en: The oven is for the main kitchen.
We paid 4,500 euros for the oven.
words.note: Por expresses the exchange: money for an item.

words.es: ¿Es una reparación o una compra de activo fijo?
words.en: Is it a repair or a fixed asset purchase?

example.target: Compramos el horno a un proveedor nuevo.
example.native: We bought the oven from a new supplier.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun compra is the matching term and takes the same stem.

example.target: Clasifico cada compra por su finalidad.
example.native: I classify each purchase by its purpose.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e the c becomes qu: clasifiqué, clasifique. Clasificar en: clasifico el gasto en mantenimiento.

example.target: Registro el gasto en la cuenta correcta.
example.native: I record the expense in the correct account.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. Registrar takes the transaction as direct object and the account with en.

example.target: El horno se deprecia durante varios años.
example.native: The oven depreciates over several years.

verbs.note: Usually used with se: el horno se deprecia. Depreciar reduces an asset's recorded value over its useful life.

passage.title: Asiento del pago al proveedor
target: Nuria y Pablo revisan un asiento antes de contabilizarlo en el sistema.
Nuria: El asiento es del pago al proveedor de la harina, con fecha del 12 de marzo.
Pablo: ¿Y el importe coincide con el justificante?
Nuria: Sí, son 860 euros, que se registran en el debe de la cuenta de compras.
Pablo: Correcto, y el haber debe ser la cuenta del banco.
Nuria: Así es. Confirma la fecha contable antes de contabilizar, por favor.
Pablo: Confirmado. Se contabilizan los asientos al cierre del día.
native: Nuria and Pablo review an entry before posting it in the system.
Nuria: The entry is for the payment to the flour supplier, dated 12 March.
Pablo: And does the amount match the supporting document?
Nuria: Yes, it is 860 euros, which are recorded on the debit side of the purchases account.
Pablo: Correct, and the credit side should be the bank account.
Nuria: That's right. Please confirm the accounting date before posting.
Pablo: Confirmed. The entries are posted at the close of the day.

words.note: A record of debits and credits for one transaction.
One line of an entry or a document.
The left column of an entry.
The right column of an entry.
The date on which a transaction is recorded in the books.
A money figure on a document.
Evidence that supports a recorded transaction.
An account number or name in the accounts.
To record a transaction in the accounts.
A check of a record before it is posted or closed.

words.es: Se registra el pago en la cuenta del proveedor.
words.en: The payment is recorded in the supplier's account.
Does the amount match the supporting document?

words.es: Confirma la fecha contable antes de contabilizar.
words.en: Please confirm the accounting date before posting.
words.note: Tú command, usual between coworkers. With a client: confirme.

words.es: Se contabilizan los asientos al cierre del día.
words.en: The entries are posted at the end of the day.

example.target: Contabilizo el asiento cuando el justificante está completo.
example.native: I post the entry when the supporting document is complete.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e the z becomes c: contabilicé, contabilice. It means to post a transaction to the books.

example.target: Registramos el pago el mismo día.
example.native: We record the payment the same day.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use registrar with a direct object (el pago) and an optional time phrase.

example.target: Reviso cada partida antes de cerrar el mes.
example.native: I review every line item before closing the month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Antes de plus an infinitive means before doing something.

example.target: El importe coincide con el recibo.
example.native: The amount matches the receipt.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. The third-person form coincide agrees with the subject: el importe coincide, los importes coinciden.

passage.title: Una entrada en el libro mayor
target: Iván pregunta a Carmen por una línea del libro mayor que no entiende.
Iván: ¿Cuál era el saldo antes del asiento de la cuenta de clientes?
Carmen: El saldo inicial era de 5.000 euros, porque el cliente todavía debía todo.
Iván: Y el cobro que aparece el martes, ¿cuándo llegó en realidad?
Carmen: El cobro llegó el lunes, pero lo anoté el martes.
Iván: Entonces el saldo final bajó a 3.800 euros después del cobro de 1.200 euros.
Carmen: Exacto, y conciliamos esa cifra con el extracto antes del cierre.
native: Iván asks Carmen about a ledger line he does not understand.
Iván: What was the balance in the receivables account before the entry?
Carmen: The opening balance was 5,000 euros, because the client still owed all of it.
Iván: And the collection shown on Tuesday, when did it actually arrive?
Carmen: The payment arrived on Monday, but I noted it on Tuesday.
Iván: So the closing balance dropped to 3,800 euros after the 1,200-euro collection.
Carmen: Exactly, and we will reconcile that figure with the statement before the close.

words.note: The record of every account and its movements.
A recorded line in a ledger.
The balance at the start of a period.
The balance at the end of a period.
A change posted to an account.
Money owed to the business by its clients.
Money received against an amount owed.
Money paid out or applied to a bill.
To match one record against another.
A change to correct or update a balance.

words.es: ¿Cuál era el saldo antes del asiento?
words.en: What was the balance before the entry?

example.target: Concilio las cuentas cada mes.
example.native: I reconcile the accounts every month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The stem concili- stays the same in every form, and conciliación is the matching noun.

example.target: Anoto cada movimiento en el libro mayor.
example.native: I note every movement in the ledger.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Anotar is common for entering a figure in a record, especially a manual record.

example.target: El cliente pagó 1.200 euros el lunes.
example.native: The client paid 1,200 euros on Monday.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. The preterite pagó marks a completed event; before e it adds u: pagué, pague.

example.target: El cliente debía todo el saldo inicial.
example.native: The client owed the whole opening balance.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Debía is the imperfect form for a past state, used to describe the amount owed before the payment.

passage.title: La factura y el pago no coinciden
target: Renata llama a la clienta Marisol Peña porque una factura aparece como pendiente.
Marisol: Pagamos la factura del mes pasado, ya hicimos la transferencia.
Renata: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia del banco.
Renata: El pago ya ha llegado, pero la referencia no coincide con la factura.
Marisol: ¿Y el importe? Transferimos exactamente el total.
Renata: El importe sí coincide, y la fecha de valor es el 3 de abril; por eso el sistema no lo asignó.
Marisol: Entonces ¿qué hacemos con la discrepancia?
Renata: Envíeme el justificante bancario y hoy mismo aplico el cobro a su factura.
native: Renata calls the client Marisol Peña because an invoice appears as outstanding.
Marisol: We paid last month's invoice, we already made the transfer.
Renata: I have compared the invoice number with the bank reference.
Renata: The payment has already arrived, but the reference does not match the invoice.
Marisol: And the amount? We transferred exactly the total.
Renata: The amount does match, and the value date is 3 April; that is why the system did not match it.
Marisol: So what do we do about the discrepancy?
Renata: Send me the bank confirmation, and today I will apply the payment to your invoice.

words.note: The identifier printed on the invoice.
The code or note that links a payment to an invoice.
A money figure on a document.
The date on which funds count for interest or availability.
A difference between two records that should match.
The act of matching records.
Money received against an invoice.
An invoice still unpaid or unmatched.
Evidence from the bank that a payment was sent or received.
A bank account for daily payments.

words.es: He comparado el número de factura con la referencia.
words.en: I have compared the invoice number with the reference.
Does the amount match the invoice?

words.es: El pago ya ha llegado con otra fecha.
words.en: The payment has already arrived with a different date.

words.es: La referencia no coincide con la factura.
words.en: The reference does not match the invoice.

example.target: Comparo la factura con el extracto.
example.native: I compare the invoice with the statement.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Comparar con means to compare with; comparar a means to compare to.

example.target: Verifico la referencia antes de confirmar.
example.native: I verify the reference before confirming.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Verificar takes a direct object. The noun verificación is the matching term.

example.target: El pago llegó el lunes.
example.native: The payment arrived on Monday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb in the present. The preterite llegó is a completed event; the present perfect ha llegado links it to now.

example.target: Transfiero el importe a la cuenta del proveedor.
example.native: I transfer the amount to the supplier's account.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie in the singular and ellos forms (transfiero, transfieren). Nosotros keeps the e: transferimos.

passage.title: Factura vencida y servicio disputado
target: Estela llama a un cliente porque una factura lleva treinta y cinco días vencida.
Estela: El plazo de pago ya venció. ¿Cuándo espera pagar la factura?
Cliente: Queremos pagar, pero hay una partida disputada que no aceptamos.
Estela: ¿Cuál es el servicio no prestado que menciona?
Cliente: La visita de mantenimiento de marzo, que nunca se hizo.
Estela: Propongo que pague ahora la parte no disputada y que revisemos esa partida por separado.
Cliente: De acuerdo. Pagaremos la parte no disputada el lunes.
Estela: Perfecto; espero que el pago llegue el martes, y antes del viernes le confirmo por escrito lo de la visita.
native: Estela calls a client because an invoice has been overdue for thirty-five days.
Estela: The payment term has already passed. When do you expect to pay the invoice?
Client: We want to pay, but there is a disputed line that we do not accept.
Estela: Which undelivered service do you mean?
Client: The March maintenance visit, which never took place.
Estela: I suggest that you pay the undisputed part now and that we review that line separately.
Client: Agreed. We will pay the undisputed part on Monday.
Estela: Perfect; I hope the payment arrives on Tuesday, and before Friday I will confirm the visit question to you in writing.

words.note: An invoice past its due date.
A line item the client disagrees with.
The part of the amount the client accepts.
The date the payment is expected.
A message asking for payment.
The time allowed to pay an invoice.
Interest charged on an overdue invoice where the law or contract allows.
A plan with agreed dates for paying an amount.
A service that was billed but not provided.
The person or business that owes the payment.

words.en: When do you expect to pay the invoice?

words.es: Espero que el pago llegue antes del viernes.
words.en: I hope the payment arrives before Friday.

words.es: Pagaremos la parte no disputada el lunes.
words.en: We will pay the undisputed part on Monday.
We will review that line separately.

example.target: No cobramos una visita que no se hizo.
example.native: We do not charge for a visit that did not take place.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Cobrar a un cliente means to charge or collect from a client; pagar is the client's side.

example.target: Reclamo el importe de la visita no realizada.
example.native: I claim the amount for the visit that was not carried out.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Reclamar means to request payment or to contest a charge, depending on the context.

example.target: La factura vence el 30 de abril.
example.native: The invoice falls due on 30 April.

verbs.note: Spelling change in the yo form (venzo, c to z). Vencer is used for due dates and expired terms; vencido is the matching adjective for an overdue item.

example.target: Espero que el cliente pague la parte acordada.
example.native: I hope the client pays the agreed part.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In the present subjunctive the g changes to gu before e (pague, paguen), which is why espero que takes pague.

passage.title: Revisión de facturas antes de pagar
target: Rosa Espinal revisa tres facturas con el dueño del restaurante antes del lote de pagos del viernes.
Rosa: Pagaremos cuando usted apruebe cada factura; empecemos por la del proveedor de carne.
Rosa: El beneficiario es la distribuidora Carnes del Norte, y el importe es de 1.840 euros.
Dueño: ¿Y la fecha de vencimiento? No quiero pagar tarde.
Rosa: Vence el 20 de noviembre; por eso la aprobación debe darse esta semana.
Dueño: Apruebo la de la carne, pero no la del servicio de limpieza hasta revisarla.
Dueño: La tercera, la del gas, también está bien, porque el importe coincide con el contrato.
Rosa: Recuerde que no se paga ninguna factura sin aprobación; dejo la de limpieza como pendiente y autorizamos el lote con las otras dos.
native: Rosa Espinal reviews three invoices with the restaurant owner before the Friday payment run.
Rosa: We will pay when you approve each invoice; let's start with the meat supplier's.
Rosa: The payee is the distributor Carnes del Norte, and the amount is 1,840 euros.
Owner: And the due date? I do not want to pay late.
Rosa: It is due on 20 November, so the approval must be given this week.
Owner: I approve the meat invoice, but not the cleaning service one until I review it.
Owner: The third one, the gas bill, is also fine, because the amount matches the contract.
Rosa: Remember that no invoice is paid without approval; I will leave the cleaning one as pending, and we will authorize the run with the other two.

words.note: The person or business that receives the payment.
The day a payment must be made.
The authorization that allows a payment to proceed.
The money figure on the bill.
A document requesting payment for goods or services.
A group of payments released together.
The instruction that authorizes a payment.
An amount held back from a payment for tax or other reasons, where applicable.
A formal permission to pay or spend.
A business that provides goods or services.

words.es: Pagaremos cuando usted apruebe la factura.
words.en: We will pay when you approve the invoice.

words.es: ¿Quién es el beneficiario de este pago?
words.en: Who is the payee of this payment?

words.es: No se paga ninguna factura sin aprobación.
words.en: No invoice is paid without approval.

words.es: Confirme el importe y la fecha de vencimiento.
words.en: Please confirm the amount and the due date.

example.target: Usted aprueba la factura antes del viernes.
example.native: You approve the invoice before Friday.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in the singular and ellos forms (apruebo, aprueba, aprueban). Nosotros keeps the o: aprobamos. The subjunctive apruebe also uses this stem.

example.target: Autorizo el lote de pagos del viernes.
example.native: I authorize the payment run for Friday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Autorizar takes a direct object; it is often used with a payment or release.

example.target: Pagaremos cuando la factura esté aprobada.
example.native: We will pay when the invoice is approved.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. After cuando, a future trigger takes the subjunctive: esté, apruebe.

example.target: Esta factura vence el 20 de noviembre.
example.native: This invoice falls due on 20 November.

verbs.note: Spelling change in the yo form (venzo). The date follows the verb directly, without a preposition.

passage.title: Conciliar el saldo del banco
target: Lucas prepara con su compañera Gloria la conciliación bancaria del restaurante antes del cierre de mes.
Gloria: El extracto muestra un saldo bancario de 9.000 euros, pero el saldo contable es de 7.930 euros.
Lucas: Gran parte de la diferencia se debe a dos cheques pendientes de cobro, de 900 y 600 euros.
Gloria: ¿Y el banco ya registró el abono del depósito de 400 euros que hicimos el día 30?
Lucas: Todavía no; aparecerá en el próximo extracto, así que es otra partida pendiente.
Gloria: ¿Hay algo en el extracto que no esté en el libro mayor?
Lucas: Sí, un cargo de 30 euros de comisión, y el saldo contable necesita ese ajuste.
Gloria: Entonces los dos saldos ajustados coinciden en 7.900 euros.
Lucas: Exacto; registramos el ajuste de la comisión después de revisar el extracto completo.
native: Lucas prepares the restaurant's bank reconciliation with his coworker Gloria before the month-end close.
Gloria: The statement shows a bank balance of 9,000 euros, but the book balance is 7,930 euros.
Lucas: Much of the difference is due to two outstanding checks, for 900 and 600 euros.
Gloria: And has the bank already recorded the credit for the 400-euro deposit we made on the 30th?
Lucas: Not yet; it will appear on the next statement, so it is another outstanding item.
Gloria: Is there anything on the statement that is not in the ledger?
Lucas: Yes, a 30-euro fee charge, and the book balance needs that adjustment.
Gloria: So the two adjusted balances agree at 7,900 euros.
Lucas: Exactly; we will record the fee adjustment after reviewing the full statement.

words.note: The process of matching a bank statement to the ledger.
A check written but not yet cleared by the bank.
A transaction in the ledger or statement that has not yet appeared on the other side.
A sum added to an account.
A sum taken from an account.
The gap between two figures.
The balance shown by the bank.
The balance shown in the ledger.
A correction made in the ledger.
The summary of the bank account for a period.

words.es: La diferencia se debe a dos cheques pendientes.
words.en: The difference is due to two outstanding checks.

words.es: El saldo bancario no coincide con el contable.
words.en: The bank balance does not match the book balance.

words.es: ¿Cuáles son las partidas pendientes de este mes?
words.en: What are the outstanding items for this month?

words.es: Registramos el ajuste después de revisar el extracto.
words.en: We record the adjustment after reviewing the statement.

example.target: Concilio el extracto con el libro mayor.
example.native: I reconcile the statement with the ledger.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The stem concili- stays the same in every form, and conciliación is the matching noun.

example.target: Registramos el abono cuando el banco lo confirma.
example.native: We record the credit when the bank confirms it.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. After cuando the subjunctive appears only when the event is future; here the verb is in the present as a habit.

example.target: El extracto muestra el saldo final.
example.native: The statement shows the closing balance.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in the singular and ellos forms (muestro, muestra, muestran). Nosotros keeps the o: mostramos.

example.target: El banco debita la comisión mensual.
example.native: The bank debits the monthly fee.

verbs.note: Common in Latin America for charging an account; Spain usually says cargar. In bookkeeping it can also mean to enter an amount on the debit side.

passage.title: Corregir un asiento duplicado
target: Elisa explica una corrección del asiento del martes a su compañera Irene.
Irene: Vi una corrección en el asiento del martes. ¿Qué pasó?
Elisa: Cuando llegó el extracto, el pago de 450 euros ya se había registrado dos veces por un error de copia.
Irene: ¿Y cuándo se detectó la partida duplicada?
Elisa: Se detectó en la revisión del cierre, al comparar el libro mayor con el extracto.
Irene: ¿Y cómo se corrige?
Elisa: Hacemos un asiento de reversión por el importe duplicado y la nota de corrección explica el cambio.
Irene: Perfecto. Con la reversión de 450 euros, confirmo el saldo revisado.
native: Elisa explains a correction to the Tuesday entry to her colleague Irene.
Irene: I saw a correction on Tuesday's entry. What happened?
Elisa: When the statement arrived, the 450-euro payment had already been recorded twice because of a copying error.
Irene: And when was the duplicate line detected?
Elisa: It was detected in the closing review, when we compared the ledger with the statement.
Irene: And how is it corrected?
Elisa: We make a reversing entry for the duplicated amount, and the correction note explains the change.
Irene: Perfect. With the 450-euro reversal, I confirm the revised balance.

words.note: The first entry before a correction.
A change that fixes an error in the records.
A mistake in entering a transaction.
An entry that cancels an earlier entry. Spain often says contraasiento or asiento de anulación.
An item recorded more than once.
The right figure after review.
A written explanation of the change.
A check of an entry or record.
A balance after the correction.
The end of an accounting period.

words.es: El asiento original registró el importe dos veces.
words.en: The original entry recorded the amount twice.

words.es: Hacemos un asiento de reversión por el importe duplicado.
words.en: We make a reversing entry for the duplicated amount.

words.es: La nota de corrección explica el cambio.
words.en: The correction note explains the change.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el saldo revisado después del ajuste?
words.en: What is the revised balance after the adjustment?

example.target: Corrijo el asiento y dejo una nota.
example.native: I correct the entry and leave a note.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (corriges, corrige, corrigen), and g becomes j before o: corrijo. Nosotros keeps the e: corregimos.

example.target: Detectamos la partida duplicada en la revisión.
example.native: We detected the duplicate line in the review.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The matching noun detección is less common than the verb in everyday accounting.

example.target: Reviso el asiento antes de cerrar.
example.native: I review the entry before closing.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Antes de plus an infinitive means before doing something.

example.target: El asiento registró el pago dos veces.
example.native: The entry recorded the payment twice.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The preterite registró is the completed event, while había registrado is the earlier action.

passage.title: Recibo de nómina de marzo
target: Verónica explica a un empleado nuevo un recibo de nómina ficticio de una empresa en España.
Empleado: ¿Por qué el sueldo neto es menor que el bruto?
Verónica: Porque se descuentan las cotizaciones a la Seguridad Social y la retención de impuestos del IRPF.
Empleado: ¿Y las horas extra también entran en el sueldo bruto?
Verónica: Sí; con las horas extra, el sueldo bruto de este recibo de nómina de marzo es de 1.200 euros.
Empleado: Entonces el neto es menos de mil euros, ¿verdad?
Verónica: Así es: se descuentan 260 euros en total, y el neto es de 940 euros.
Empleado: Gracias; ahora compruebo si las horas extra del recibo coinciden con mis horas.
native: Verónica explains a fictional payslip from a company in Spain to a new employee.
Employee: Why is the net pay less than the gross pay?
Verónica: Because the Social Security contributions and the IRPF income tax withholding are deducted.
Employee: And the overtime is also part of the gross pay?
Verónica: Yes; with the overtime, the gross pay on this March payslip is 1,200 euros.
Employee: So the net is less than a thousand euros, right?
Verónica: That's right: 260 euros are deducted in total, and the net is 940 euros.
Employee: Thank you; now I will check whether the overtime on the payslip matches my hours.

words.note: Pay before deductions.
Pay after deductions, the amount transferred.
An amount subtracted from gross pay.
In Spain, cotización a la Seguridad Social. Aporte is common in parts of Latin America.
An amount withheld from pay for tax. On a payslip in Spain it is the IRPF withholding.
Hours worked beyond the agreed schedule.
The statement showing pay and deductions for a period.
The time covered by one payment.
A person who works under an employment relationship.
The system and list of wages.

words.es: El sueldo neto es menor que el bruto.
words.en: The net pay is less than the gross pay.

words.es: Se descuenta la cotización a la Seguridad Social.
words.en: The Social Security contribution is deducted.

words.es: ¿Coinciden las horas con el recibo de nómina?
words.en: Do the hours match the payslip?

words.es: El importe neto llega a su cuenta.
words.en: The net amount reaches your account.

example.target: La empresa descuenta la cotización del salario bruto.
example.native: The company deducts the contribution from the gross salary.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in the singular and ellos forms (descuento, descuenta, descuentan). Nosotros keeps the o: descontamos.

example.target: La empresa paga el sueldo el último día del mes.
example.native: The company pays the salary on the last day of the month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Pagar takes the salary as direct object and the employee as indirect object with le.

example.target: Calculo el neto restando los descuentos.
example.native: I calculate the net pay by subtracting the deductions.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Calcular takes the result as direct object; restando is the gerund that gives the method.

example.target: El empleado cobra el sueldo cada mes.
example.native: The employee receives pay every month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. For an employee, cobrar means to be paid, which is the opposite perspective of pagar.

passage.title: Contratista o empleada
target: Beatriz, asesora laboral en Madrid, pregunta a un cliente cómo está clasificada una diseñadora gráfica.
Cliente: Ella trabaja con nosotros desde enero, pero no sé si es empleada.
Beatriz: ¿Es autónoma y les emite una factura de servicios cada mes?
Cliente: Factura cada mes, pero el contrato dice que está en nómina.
Beatriz: Entonces la clasificación laboral necesita revisarse: hay que comparar el contrato con la forma real de trabajo.
Cliente: ¿Qué documentos debo enviarle?
Beatriz: El contrato firmado, las facturas de servicios de los últimos seis meses y, si está en nómina, sus recibos de nómina.
Beatriz: Con eso, el lunes lo reviso con nuestra especialista laboral y le digo el siguiente paso.
native: Beatriz, an employment adviser in Madrid, asks a client how a graphic designer is classified.
Client: She has worked with us since January, but I do not know if she is an employee.
Beatriz: Is she self-employed, and does she issue you a services invoice every month?
Client: She invoices every month, but the contract says she is on payroll.
Beatriz: Then the employment classification needs review: we have to compare the contract with how she actually works.
Client: Which documents should I send you?
Beatriz: The signed contract, the services invoices for the last six months and, if she is on payroll, her payslips.
Beatriz: With that, on Monday I will review it with our employment specialist and tell you the next step.

words.note: A person or business that performs work under a service agreement.
A person working under an employment contract.
A person who works for their own account, the term used in Spain and some other countries.
An agreement for a defined service rather than employment.
An agreement that creates an employment relationship.
An invoice a contractor issues for work performed.
The list of employees paid through wages.
A contract or rule that currently applies.
The decision about whether a worker is an employee or a contractor.
The records that describe the arrangement.

words.es: ¿Es empleada o trabaja por cuenta propia?
words.en: Is she an employee or does she work for her own account?

words.es: Necesitamos el contrato y las facturas de servicios.
words.en: We need the contract and the services invoices.

words.es: El contrato está vigente desde enero.
words.en: The contract has been in force since January.

words.es: La clasificación depende de la jurisdicción.
words.en: The classification depends on the jurisdiction.

example.target: La diseñadora trabaja por cuenta propia.
example.native: The designer works for her own account.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The phrase por cuenta propia is the usual Spanish expression for self-employment in many countries.

example.target: Ella factura sus servicios cada mes.
example.native: She invoices her services each month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Factura is also the noun invoice, and the third-person form factura looks like it; context decides.

example.target: Clasificamos al trabajador según el contrato.
example.native: We classify the worker according to the contract.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e the c becomes qu: clasifiqué, clasifique. It takes a personal a with a person: clasificar al trabajador.

example.target: Le envío el contrato y las facturas.
example.native: I will send you the contract and the invoices.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The indirect pronoun le names the person receiving the documents.

passage.title: Resultados de la panadería
target: Clara revisa el estado de resultados de la panadería con su dueño.
Dueño: ¿Ganamos más de lo que gastamos en el trimestre?
Clara: Sí: los ingresos fueron de 42.000 euros y los gastos de 36.500, así que la utilidad es de 5.500 euros, menor que la del año pasado.
Dueño: ¿Y las ventas netas son tan altas como las del trimestre anterior?
Clara: No, son menores, porque hubo devoluciones y descuentos en las fiestas.
Dueño: ¿El costo de ventas explica la baja del margen?
Clara: En parte; el gasto operativo también subió, así que no ganamos tanto como esperábamos.
native: Clara reviews the bakery's income statement with its owner.
Owner: Did we earn more than we spent in the quarter?
Clara: Yes: revenue was 42,000 euros and expenses 36,500, so the profit is 5,500 euros, lower than last year's.
Owner: And are net sales as high as last quarter's?
Clara: No, they are lower, because there were returns and holiday discounts.
Owner: Does the cost of sales explain the lower margin?
Clara: Partly; operating expense also rose, so we did not earn as much as we expected.

words.note: Money earned from sales or services in a period.
Costs incurred in a period.
What remains after expenses are subtracted from revenue. Common in Latin America; Spain usually says beneficio.
A report of revenue, expenses and profit for a period.
The time covered by the report.
The share of revenue that remains as profit.
The direct cost of the goods or services sold.
A cost of running the business that is not a direct cost of sales.
Sales after returns and discounts.
The outcome, such as a profit or loss.

words.es: Los ingresos son mayores que los gastos.

words.en: We did not earn as much as we expected.
words.note: Tanto como follows a verb. With an adjective use tan ... como.

words.en: What does the income statement include?

words.es: El margen es menor este trimestre.
words.en: The margin is lower this quarter.

example.target: El estado de resultados incluye los ingresos del periodo.
example.native: The income statement includes the revenue for the period.

verbs.note: Incluir adds y before the ending in every form except nosotros: incluyo, incluyes, incluye, incluyen; incluimos.

example.target: Los gastos operativos suben este trimestre.
example.native: Operating expenses rise this quarter.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. Subir means to rise or increase; with the object (precio) it means to raise a price.

example.target: Clara explica el resultado al dueño.
example.native: Clara explains the result to the owner.

verbs.note: Regular in the present; before e the c becomes qu: expliqué. The thing explained is the direct object; the listener is indirect: le explico.

example.target: Esperábamos una utilidad más alta.
example.native: We expected a higher profit.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The imperfect esperábamos describes what we expected before the result was known.

passage.title: Qué tiene y qué debe el negocio
target: Lourdes muestra el balance general de la tienda a la nueva dueña, Teresa Moya.
Lourdes: El activo total, 80.000 euros, es igual al pasivo de 30.000 más el patrimonio de 50.000.
Teresa: ¿Qué incluye el activo corriente?
Lourdes: Incluye el efectivo y las cuentas de clientes que cobraremos en los próximos meses.
Teresa: ¿Y el pasivo corriente?
Lourdes: Es lo que la tienda debe a proveedores y la parte del préstamo que vence este año.
Teresa: Entonces el patrimonio, esos 50.000 euros, es lo que queda para los dueños.
Lourdes: Exacto, y el capital social de la empresa es parte de ese patrimonio.
native: Lourdes shows the shop's balance sheet to the new owner, Teresa Moya.
Lourdes: Total assets, 80,000 euros, equal liabilities of 30,000 plus equity of 50,000.
Teresa: What do current assets include?
Lourdes: They include cash and the customer accounts we will collect in the coming months.
Teresa: And the current liabilities?
Lourdes: It is what the shop owes suppliers and the part of the loan that falls due this year.
Teresa: So equity, those 50,000 euros, is what remains for the owners.
Lourdes: Exactly, and the share capital of the company is part of that equity.

words.note: Something the business owns or controls that has value.
An obligation the business owes to others.
The owners' share after liabilities are subtracted from assets. On a balance sheet in Spain it appears as patrimonio neto.
A snapshot of assets, liabilities and equity at a date. Estado de situación financiera is used in some countries.
An asset expected to be used or converted within a year.
A long-lived asset such as equipment or a building.
An obligation due within a year.
Money borrowed under agreed terms.
Money held in hand or in a bank account for immediate use.
Capital contributed by the owners of a company.

words.es: El activo total es igual al pasivo más el patrimonio.
words.en: Total assets equal liabilities plus equity.

words.es: El pasivo corriente vence este año.
words.en: The current liabilities fall due this year.

example.target: La tienda tiene un horno y dos mesas nuevas.
example.native: The shop has a new oven and two new tables.

verbs.note: Irregular: tengo has a g, and tienes, tiene and tienen change e to ie. In accounting, tener expresses what the business holds.

example.target: La tienda debe dinero al proveedor.
example.native: The shop owes money to the supplier.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Deber without an infinitive means to owe an amount; with an infinitive it means must.

example.target: El balance cuadra con el libro mayor.
example.native: The balance sheet matches the ledger.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In bookkeeping, cuadrar means the two sides agree.

example.target: El préstamo vence el próximo año.
example.native: The loan falls due next year.

verbs.note: Spelling change in the yo form (venzo). Use vencer for a due date or term that ends.

passage.title: Utilidad sin efectivo
target: Pilar revisa el flujo de efectivo de la tienda junto con el dueño, Esteban.
Esteban: El mes salió con una utilidad de 3.000 euros, aunque el banco casi no tiene saldo.
Pilar: Eso pasa porque la utilidad no es lo mismo que el efectivo disponible.
Esteban: ¿Cuál es el problema concreto?
Pilar: Hay un cobro pendiente de 7.500 euros de una venta grande, y el proveedor cobra 4.200 euros el lunes.
Esteban: Entonces ganamos, pero el dinero todavía no entró.
Pilar: Exacto. Revisemos los pagos programados y la reserva antes de comprometer más compras.
Esteban: Entendido: la utilidad está en el informe, pero el efectivo llega cuando el cliente paga.
native: Pilar reviews the shop's cash flow with its owner, Esteban.
Esteban: The month showed a profit of 3,000 euros, although the bank balance is almost zero.
Pilar: That happens because profit is not the same as the cash available.
Esteban: What is the specific problem?
Pilar: There is an outstanding collection of 7,500 euros from a large sale, and the supplier is due 4,200 euros on Monday.
Esteban: So we made money, but the cash has not come in yet.
Pilar: Exactly. Let's review the scheduled payments and the reserve before committing more purchases.
Esteban: Understood: the profit is on the report, but the cash arrives when the customer pays.

words.note: The movement of cash into and out of the business over a period.
The recorded result after expenses.
Money that can be used now.
An amount a client owes to the business.
An amount the business owes a supplier.
A sale recorded but not yet paid.
A payment set for a date.
The money needed to cover daily operations.
The ability to pay obligations as they come due.
Money set aside for a future need.

words.es: Aunque ganamos dinero, no tenemos efectivo suficiente.
words.en: Although we made money, we do not have enough cash.

words.es: La utilidad no es lo mismo que el efectivo disponible.
words.en: Profit is not the same as the cash available.

words.es: Hay un cobro pendiente de la semana pasada.
words.en: There is a collection outstanding from last week.

words.es: ¿Qué pagos están programados para este mes?
words.en: Which payments are scheduled for this month?

example.target: La tienda cobra la venta a 30 días.
example.native: The shop collects the sale at 30 days.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Cobrar is the matching verb for a receivable and cobro pendiente.

example.target: Pagamos al proveedor el lunes.
example.native: We pay the supplier on Monday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb with no change in the present. The future pagaremos is built on the infinitive pagar.

example.target: No comprometemos más compras sin revisar el efectivo.
example.native: We do not commit to more purchases without reviewing the cash.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Comprometer plus a direct object means to commit money or resources, and comprometerse con means to commit oneself to something.

example.target: El dinero entra cuando el cliente paga.
example.native: The money comes in when the client pays.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In cash-flow language, entrar means money coming in and salir means money going out.

passage.title: Presupuesto para una camioneta
target: Andrea y Hugo preparan el presupuesto del próximo trimestre para el servicio de entregas.
Hugo: Quiero comprar una furgoneta; ¿cuánto esperamos vender?
Andrea: Los ingresos previstos son de 18.000 euros, según el supuesto de volumen de entregas.
Hugo: ¿Y los costos fijos y variables?
Andrea: Los fijos son 6.500 euros de alquiler y personal; los variables, unos 3.000 euros de combustible y peajes.
Andrea: Con ese escenario, el margen previsto es de unos 8.500 euros antes de la compra planificada.
Hugo: Si vendemos más de lo previsto, podremos comprar la furgoneta antes de junio.
Andrea: Vamos a revisar el presupuesto a fin de mes para confirmar ese escenario y el flujo de efectivo.
native: Andrea and Hugo prepare next quarter's budget for the delivery service.
Hugo: I want to buy a van; how much do we expect to sell?
Andrea: Expected revenue is 18,000 euros, based on the delivery volume assumption.
Hugo: And the fixed and variable costs?
Andrea: The fixed costs are 6,500 euros for rent and staff; the variable ones, about 3,000 euros for fuel and tolls.
Andrea: In that scenario, the expected margin is about 8,500 euros before the planned purchase.
Hugo: If we sell more than expected, we will be able to buy the van before June.
Andrea: We are going to review the budget at the end of the month to confirm that scenario and the cash flow.

words.note: A plan of expected revenue and costs for a period.
Revenue the plan expects to earn.
Costs that do not change with sales volume, such as rent. Spain also says costes fijos.
Costs that change with sales volume, such as fuel for deliveries.
A purchase included in the budget before it is made.
An expectation the plan depends on.
One possible case the plan is tested against.
Cash coming in and going out over a period.
A light commercial van, the usual word in Spain. Much of Latin America says camioneta.
A transfer of goods to a customer.

words.en: How much do we expect to sell next quarter?

words.es: Si vendemos más, podremos comprar la furgoneta.
words.en: If we sell more, we will be able to buy the van.

words.es: Vamos a revisar el presupuesto a fin de mes.
words.en: We are going to review the budget at month end.

words.es: El supuesto principal es el volumen de entregas.
words.en: The main assumption is the volume of deliveries.

example.target: Planeamos el presupuesto con dos escenarios.
example.native: We plan the budget with two scenarios.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Planear is common in everyday speech; planificar is the more formal synonym in many countries.

example.target: Preveo un aumento de las entregas.
example.native: I foresee an increase in deliveries.

verbs.note: Irregular like ver in the yo form (preveo). The tú and él forms carry an accent (prevés, prevé); the nosotros and ellos forms are prevemos and prevén.

example.target: Vendemos más en el segundo trimestre.
example.native: We sell more in the second quarter.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. The future form venderemos is built on the infinitive vender plus -emos.

example.target: Compraremos la furgoneta cuando el presupuesto lo permita.
example.native: We will buy the van when the budget allows it.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use comprar for the purchase itself; the planned form is vamos a comprar.

passage.title: Gasto de entregas por encima del plan
target: Luisa, la gerente, revisa la variación del gasto de entregas con su contador, Nacho.
Luisa: El gasto real es superior al presupuestado; ¿cuál es la causa?
Nacho: El gasto subió porque el combustible costó más de lo previsto.
Luisa: ¿Y cuánto representa la variación en el presupuesto del mes?
Nacho: El presupuesto era de 2.400 euros y el gasto real fue de 3.300, una desviación de 900 euros debido al precio del diésel.
Luisa: ¿La variación va a continuar el próximo mes?
Nacho: Revisaremos el pronóstico la próxima semana para saber si el sobrecosto continúa.
Luisa: De acuerdo, y mientras tanto agrupamos las entregas por zona para gastar menos combustible.
native: Luisa, the manager, reviews the delivery expense variance with her accountant, Nacho.
Luisa: The actual expense is higher than budgeted; what is the cause?
Nacho: The expense rose because fuel cost more than expected.
Luisa: And how large is the variance in this month's budget?
Nacho: The budget was 2,400 euros and the actual expense was 3,300, a deviation of 900 euros due to the price of diesel.
Luisa: Is the variance going to continue next month?
Nacho: We will review the forecast next week to see whether the overrun continues.
Luisa: Agreed, and in the meantime we will group deliveries by area to use less fuel.

words.note: The difference between planned and actual amounts.
The amount actually spent.
The amount planned in the budget.
Gasoline or diesel used by vehicles.
A departure from the plan.
The reason for a difference.
A change made to correct the plan or the record.
An amount above the budget. Spain also says sobrecoste.
One item in a budget or report.
An updated estimate of the future.

words.es: El gasto real es superior al presupuestado.
words.en: The actual expense is higher than budgeted.

words.es: ¿Cuál es la causa de la variación?
words.en: What is the cause of the variance?

words.es: El gasto subió porque el combustible costó más.
words.en: The expense rose because fuel cost more.

words.es: Revisaremos el pronóstico la próxima semana.
words.en: We will review the forecast next week.

example.target: El precio del combustible sube este mes.
example.native: The price of fuel rises this month.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb in the present (subo, subes, suben). Subir means to rise or increase, so the subject is the figure that goes up.

example.target: El combustible cuesta más de lo previsto.
example.native: The fuel costs more than expected.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in the singular and ellos forms (cuesto, cuesta, cuestan). Nosotros keeps the o: costamos.

example.target: Revisamos la variación cada mes.
example.native: We review the variance each month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Revisar takes a direct object, usually the figures under review.

example.target: Explico la causa de la desviación.
example.native: I explain the cause of the deviation.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Explicar takes the explained item as direct object and the listener as indirect object.

passage.title: Actualización del mes
target: Patricia redacta la actualización mensual para su cliente, el señor Dávila.
Patricia: Hemos recibido todos los extractos del mes y hemos revisado las facturas.
Patricia: El resultado principal es una utilidad mayor que la del mes anterior.
Patricia: Queda una pregunta pendiente: necesitamos saber si la factura del proveedor de limpieza corresponde a marzo o a abril.
Dávila: ¿Cuál es la próxima acción?
Patricia: Vamos a enviar el informe final el jueves, después de la conciliación.
Patricia: ¿Podría confirmarnos esta información antes de la fecha límite del miércoles?
Dávila: Sí, se la confirmo el miércoles por la tarde y, si veo alguna corrección, se la digo antes.
native: Patricia drafts the monthly update for her client, Mr. Dávila.
Patricia: We have received all the statements for the month and reviewed the invoices.
Patricia: The main result is a profit higher than the one from the previous month.
Patricia: One question remains open: we need to know whether the cleaning supplier's invoice belongs to March or April.
Dávila: What is the next action?
Patricia: We are going to send the final report on Thursday, after the reconciliation.
Patricia: Could you confirm this information for us before the Wednesday deadline?
Dávila: Yes, I will confirm it on Wednesday afternoon, and if I see any correction, I will tell you before then.

words.note: A short client update on results and open items. Resumen mensual is also used.
An outcome for the period.
An unresolved issue that needs a client answer.
The next step with a responsible person and a date.
A written account of results.
The person receiving the update.
A bill for services or goods.
Account summary for a period.
Matching of two records.
The last date for an action.

words.es: Hemos recibido todos los extractos del mes.
words.en: We have received all the statements for the month.

words.es: Queda una pregunta pendiente sobre una factura.
words.en: One question remains open about an invoice.

words.es: Vamos a enviar el informe final el jueves.
words.en: We are going to send the final report on Thursday.

words.es: ¿Podría confirmarnos esta información antes de la fecha límite?
words.en: Could you confirm this information before the deadline?

example.target: Enviamos el informe final por correo.
example.native: We send the final report by email.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Enviar takes the document as direct object and the recipient with a or the indirect pronoun le.

example.target: He revisado las facturas del mes.
example.native: I have reviewed the invoices for the month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. The participle revisado is used with haber in the present perfect.

example.target: Le confirmo la respuesta el miércoles.
example.native: I will confirm the answer to you on Wednesday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun confirmación is the matching term for a written confirmation.

example.target: Resumo los resultados en una página.
example.native: I summarize the results on one page.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. The noun resumen is the matching word for a summary.

passage.title: Solicitud de préstamo para ampliar
target: Gerardo, gestor de empresas del banco, atiende a una panadera que quiere ampliar su local.
Gerardo: Buenos días, ¿en qué le puedo ayudar con la solicitud?
Clienta: Quisiera solicitar un préstamo para ampliar la panadería.
Gerardo: ¿Cuál es el monto solicitado y el plazo que propone?
Clienta: El monto solicitado es de 25.000 euros, en un plazo de cinco años.
Clienta: ¿Podría indicarme qué documentación necesita el banco para la revisión?
Gerardo: Los estados financieros de los dos últimos años, el presupuesto de la obra y una propuesta de garantía.
Clienta: Perfecto; se los envío el lunes y confirmamos la próxima reunión para el jueves.
native: Gerardo, a business banker, meets a baker who wants to expand her shop.
Gerardo: Good morning, how can I help you with the application?
Client: I would like to request a loan to expand the bakery.
Gerardo: What is the requested amount and the term you propose?
Client: The requested amount is 25,000 euros, over a term of five years.
Client: Could you tell me what documentation the bank needs for the review?
Gerardo: The financial statements for the last two years, the budget for the works and a proposed guarantee.
Client: Perfect; I will send them on Monday, and we will confirm the next meeting for Thursday.

words.note: A formal request to borrow money.
The amount asked for in the loan application.
The time for repayment.
The reason the money is borrowed.
A financial institution that lends money.
The documents the lender asks for.
The statements that report the business position.
Something pledged to secure the loan.
The percentage charged on the loan.
The lender's decision to grant the loan.

words.es: Quisiera solicitar un préstamo para ampliar la panadería.
words.en: I would like to request a loan to expand the bakery.

words.es: ¿Qué documentos necesita el banco para revisar la solicitud?
words.en: What documents does the bank need to review the application?

words.es: El monto solicitado es de 25.000 euros.

words.en: Could you tell me the term you propose?

example.target: Solicito un préstamo para comprar equipo.
example.native: I apply for a loan to buy equipment.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Solicitar takes a direct object (un préstamo, una cita). The noun solicitud is the matching term for the application.

example.target: Quiero ampliar el local el próximo año.
example.native: I want to expand the premises next year.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie except in nosotros: quiero, quiere, quieren; queremos. Quisiera, an imperfect subjunctive form, is the usual polite request.

example.target: Amplío el local con el préstamo.
example.native: I am expanding the premises with the loan.

verbs.note: Verbs ending in -iar stress the i in most forms (amplío, amplías, amplían). Nosotros is ampliamos, with no accent.

example.target: ¿Podría indicarme el plazo del préstamo?
example.native: Could you indicate the term of the loan to me?

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In a polite request, indicar takes the indirect pronoun me: podría indicarme.

passage.title: Cotización de un préstamo
target: Iván recibe una cotización de préstamo para su taller y la revisa con su asesora, Elena Ramos.
Iván: El capital es de 20.000 euros a cinco años, así que esperaba una cuota mensual de unos 333 euros, no de 387.
Elena: La cuota incluye capital e intereses; esta cotización indica un interés fijo del 6 % anual.
Iván: ¿Y la comisión de apertura? ¿Se suma a la cuota?
Elena: No, se paga una vez al inicio: son 200 euros, el 1 % del capital.
Iván: Entonces ¿cuál es el costo total del préstamo?
Elena: Tanto los intereses, unos 3.200 euros, como la comisión forman el costo: unos 3.400 euros además del capital.
Iván: Gracias. Quiero el cronograma de pagos antes de decidir.
native: Iván receives a loan quote for his workshop and reviews it with his adviser, Elena Ramos.
Iván: The principal is 20,000 euros over five years, so I expected a monthly payment of about 333 euros, not 387.
Elena: The payment includes principal and interest; this quote shows a fixed interest rate of 6% a year.
Iván: And the arrangement fee? Is it added to the payment?
Elena: No, it is paid once at the start: 200 euros, 1% of the principal.
Iván: So what is the total cost of the loan?
Elena: Both the interest, about 3,200 euros, and the fee make up the cost: about 3,400 euros on top of the principal.
Iván: Thank you. I want the payment schedule before I decide.

words.note: The amount borrowed, before interest is added.
The cost of borrowing money, usually shown as a rate.
The period over which the loan is repaid.
A one-time fee for setting up the loan.
The regular amount paid each month.
The table of payments and their split between capital and interest.
The yearly interest rate. Spain distinguishes TIN, the nominal rate, from TAE, the annual equivalent rate that includes some costs.
All payments added together, including fees and interest.
The part of each payment that reduces the capital owed.
A written offer with the terms of a loan.

words.es: ¿Cuánto es el costo total del préstamo?
words.en: What is the total cost of the loan?

words.es: La comisión de apertura se paga una vez.
words.en: The arrangement fee is paid once.

words.es: ¿Cómo se reparte la cuota en el cronograma?
words.en: How is the payment split in the schedule?

example.target: Usted paga la cuota cada mes.
example.native: You pay the monthly payment each month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Pagar takes the amount as direct object and the lender or the time phrase as additional information.

example.target: La cuota incluye capital e intereses.
example.native: The payment includes principal and interest.

verbs.note: The yo and third-person forms add -y before the ending. Nosotros is incluimos, which has no y.

example.target: Los intereses suman unos 3.200 euros.

example.native: The payment is split between principal and interest.

passage.title: Garantía sobre el equipo
target: Marcela trabaja en el banco prestamista y explica a Hugo, el prestatario, qué garantía acepta el banco.
Marcela: Podemos aceptar el equipo como garantía real del préstamo.
Hugo: ¿Qué cubre exactamente la garantía? Quiero saber lo que pasa si no pago.
Marcela: Cubre el saldo pendiente hasta el valor que fije la valoración del equipo.
Hugo: ¿Y el aval de mi socio también se requiere?
Marcela: Solo si la valoración no alcanza; entonces buscaríamos una garantía que cubra el resto del préstamo.
Hugo: Solicito las condiciones por escrito antes de firmar.
Marcela: Se las envío esta semana con la fecha de vencimiento de la garantía.
native: Marcela works at the lending bank and explains to Hugo, the borrower, which guarantee the bank accepts.
Marcela: We can accept the equipment as collateral for the loan.
Hugo: What exactly does the guarantee cover? I want to know what happens if I do not pay.
Marcela: It covers the outstanding balance up to the value set by the valuation of the equipment.
Hugo: And is my partner's personal guarantee also required?
Marcela: Only if the valuation falls short; then we would look for a guarantee that covers the rest of the loan.
Hugo: I am requesting the written terms before signing.
Marcela: I will send them to you this week with the date the guarantee expires.

words.note: A pledge of an asset or a third party to secure a loan.
A guarantee tied to a specific asset, such as equipment or property.
A promise by a third person to pay if the borrower cannot.
Machines or tools the business uses.
The date a guarantee or loan ends.
The conditions in a written document.
An estimate of the value of an asset.
The extent of protection the guarantee provides.
The person or business that receives the loan.
The person or institution that lends the money.

words.en: What exactly does the guarantee cover?

words.es: Necesitamos una garantía que cubra todo el préstamo.
words.en: We need a guarantee that covers the whole loan.
When does the equipment guarantee expire?

example.target: Aceptamos el equipo como garantía.
example.native: We accept the equipment as the guarantee.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Aceptar takes a direct object, usually the guarantee or the condition being accepted.

example.target: La garantía cubre el saldo pendiente.
example.native: The guarantee covers the outstanding balance.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb with the stem cubr- in every form. The subjunctive cubra is used after an unknown or indefinite guarantee.

example.target: Firmo el contrato después de revisar las condiciones.
example.native: I sign the contract after reviewing the conditions.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun firma is the matching word for a signature and also for a firm.

example.target: La valoración fija el valor del equipo.
example.native: The valuation sets the value of the equipment.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Fijar means to set a value or condition; fijo is the matching adjective meaning fixed.

passage.title: Comisión inesperada
target: Susana llama al banco porque una comisión apareció en la cuenta de negocios del taller.
Ejecutivo: Buenas tardes, ¿en qué le ayudo con la cuenta?
Susana: Hay un cargo de comisión bancaria que no esperaba; ¿qué lo motivó?
Ejecutivo: La comisión se aplicó porque el saldo bajó del mínimo la semana pasada.
Susana: ¿Se puede revisar la comisión? El saldo bajó solo un día, por una transferencia internacional que pagamos.
Ejecutivo: Sí, voy a abrir una revisión de comisión, y el banco responderá en tres días hábiles.
Susana: ¿Y si procede, se hace un reembolso?
Ejecutivo: Si corresponde, el reembolso se abona en la cuenta de negocios.
native: Susana calls the bank because a fee appeared on the workshop's business account.
Account manager: Good afternoon, how can I help you with the account?
Susana: There is a bank fee charge that I did not expect; what triggered it?
Account manager: The fee was applied because the balance fell below the minimum last week.
Susana: Can the fee be reviewed? The balance dropped for only one day, because of an international transfer we paid.
Account manager: Yes, I will open a fee review, and the bank will respond within three business days.
Susana: And if it is justified, will there be a refund?
Account manager: If it applies, the refund will be credited to the business account.

words.note: A charge by the bank for a service or condition.
A bank account for business transactions.
The lowest balance required to avoid a fee.
An amount taken from the account.
A payment sent across borders.
A return of money paid.
A check of whether a fee applies correctly.
The bank contact for a business account.
The terms that govern the account.
The published price of a banking service.

words.es: ¿Qué motivó el cargo de la comisión?
La comisión se aplicó por saldo inferior al mínimo.
words.en: The fee was applied because the balance was below the minimum.

words.es: El banco responderá en tres días hábiles.
words.en: The bank will respond in three business days.

example.target: El banco aplica la comisión según el contrato de cuenta.
example.native: The bank applies the fee under the account agreement.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e the c becomes qu: apliqué, aplique. Aplicar a means to apply something to an account.

example.target: Revisamos la comisión con el ejecutivo.
example.native: We review the fee with the account manager.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Revisar takes a direct object. Use it for a charge or a document under examination.

example.target: ¿Qué motivó la comisión?
example.native: What caused the fee?

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In a question about a cause, motivar means to cause or trigger.

example.target: El banco responde en tres días.
example.native: The bank responds within three days.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Responder a means to answer or respond to a request or message.

passage.title: Preparar la reunión fiscal
target: Ramiro, asesor fiscal en Valencia, prepara una reunión con una clienta para revisar su declaración de la renta.
Ramiro: Confirme la jurisdicción y el periodo del informe antes de la reunión, por favor.
Clienta: Es España, y es la declaración del año fiscal 2025, porque viví aquí todo el año.
Ramiro: ¿Qué documentos tiene disponibles para ese periodo?
Clienta: Tengo el certificado de retenciones de mi empresa y los recibos del alquiler, pero no el certificado de intereses del banco.
Ramiro: No olvide que necesitamos los recibos del año fiscal completo y ese certificado del banco.
Clienta: Los traeré, y también una copia de la última declaración.
Ramiro: Perfecto. Con eso revisamos todo antes del plazo de presentación que fija la Agencia Tributaria.
native: Ramiro, a tax adviser in Valencia, prepares a meeting with a client to review her income tax return.
Ramiro: Please confirm the jurisdiction and the reporting period before the meeting.
Client: It is Spain, and it is the return for tax year 2025, because I lived here all year.
Ramiro: Which documents do you have available for that period?
Client: I have my employer's withholding certificate and the rent receipts, but not the bank's interest certificate.
Ramiro: Do not forget that we need the receipts for the full tax year and that bank certificate.
Client: I will bring them, and also a copy of the last return.
Ramiro: Perfect. With that, we will review everything before the filing deadline set by the Spanish Tax Agency.

words.note: The authority whose tax rules apply.
The time covered by a tax report.
A formal filing to a tax authority. In Spain the personal income tax return is the declaración de la renta.
The annual period used for tax purposes.
Proof of payment for deductible or reportable items.
Records used for a tax filing.
The government body that collects tax. In Spain it is the Agencia Tributaria.
A professional who prepares or reviews tax filings.
The date by which a return must be submitted.
A duplicate of a document kept for the file.

words.es: Confirme la jurisdicción antes de la reunión.
words.en: Please confirm the jurisdiction before the meeting.

words.es: No olvide que necesitamos los recibos del año fiscal.
words.en: Do not forget that we need the receipts for the tax year.

words.es: ¿Qué documentos tiene disponibles para el periodo?
words.en: Which documents do you have available for the period?

words.es: Traiga la copia de la última declaración.
words.en: Bring a copy of the last return.

example.target: Preparo la declaración con sus recibos.
example.native: I prepare the return with her receipts.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The usted command prepare is formal; the present form is prepara for él, ella and usted.

example.target: Confirmo la jurisdicción con la clienta.
example.native: I confirm the jurisdiction with the client.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun confirmación is the matching word for a confirmation.

example.native: Bring the copy of the return.

verbs.note: Irregular only in the yo form (traigo). The usted command traiga uses the same stem.

example.native: We file the return before the deadline.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Presentar a return means to submit it to the tax authority.

passage.title: Deducción y crédito en un ejemplo
target: Marta, preparadora de impuestos en Houston, explica a un cliente la diferencia entre una deducción y un crédito tributario en la declaración federal.
Cliente: ¿Son lo mismo? Los dos bajan el impuesto, ¿no?
Marta: No: una deducción reduce la base imponible, y un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente.
Cliente: ¿Cómo se ve eso con números?
Marta: En un ejemplo ficticio con una tasa impositiva del 20 %, una deducción de 1.000 dólares ahorra 200 dólares de impuesto.
Cliente: ¿Y un crédito de 1.000 dólares?
Marta: Reduce el impuesto a pagar en 1.000 dólares, así que vale más que una deducción del mismo importe.
Cliente: Entendido: con la misma cifra, la deducción vale menos que el crédito.
Marta: Exacto, y con sus documentos confirmaremos qué deducciones y créditos le corresponden de verdad.
native: Marta, a tax preparer in Houston, explains to a client the difference between a deduction and a tax credit on the federal return.
Client: Are they the same? Both lower the tax, don't they?
Marta: No: a deduction reduces the taxable base, and a credit reduces the tax directly.
Client: How does that look with numbers?
Marta: In a fictional example with a 20% tax rate, a 1,000-dollar deduction saves 200 dollars of tax.
Client: And a 1,000-dollar credit?
Marta: It reduces the tax payable by 1,000 dollars, so it is worth more than a deduction of the same amount.
Client: Understood: for the same figure, the deduction is worth less than the credit.
Marta: Exactly, and with your documents we will confirm which deductions and credits actually apply to you.

words.note: On a US return it lowers taxable income. In Spain's IRPF, deducción lowers the tax itself and reducción lowers the base.
An amount subtracted from the tax owed. IRS Spanish materials say crédito tributario; crédito fiscal is also common.
The amount on which tax is calculated.
The percentage applied to the taxable base.
The tax amount owed after credits.
A cost the tax rules allow to be deducted. Which costs qualify depends on the jurisdiction and the taxpayer.
The authority whose rules apply.
A teaching case that does not describe a real rule.
A decrease in an amount. In Spain's IRPF, reducciones lower the taxable base, while deducciones lower the tax itself.
The final calculation of tax owed.

words.es: Una deducción reduce la base imponible.
words.en: A deduction reduces the taxable base.

words.es: Un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente.
words.en: A credit reduces the tax directly.

words.es: Con la misma cifra, la deducción vale menos que el crédito.
words.en: For the same figure, the deduction is worth less than the credit.

words.es: Este es un ejemplo ficticio, no una regla real.
words.en: This is a fictional example, not a real rule.

example.target: Una deducción reduce la base imponible.
example.native: A deduction reduces the taxable base.

verbs.note: Irregular only in the yo form (reduzco, with zc). The other forms are regular: reduces, reduce, reducimos, reducen.

example.target: Calculamos el impuesto sobre la base imponible.
example.native: We calculate the tax on the taxable base.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun cálculo is the matching term for a calculation.

example.target: Una deducción ahorra impuesto al cliente.
example.native: A deduction saves the client tax.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Ahorrar can mean to save money, or to avoid paying an amount.

example.target: Un crédito de 1.000 dólares vale más que la deducción.
example.native: A 1,000-dollar credit is worth more than the deduction.

verbs.note: Irregular in the yo form (valgo, the g). The other persons are regular: vales, vale, valen; nosotros is valemos.

passage.title: Pagos estimados del año
target: Fernando, autónomo en Sevilla, pregunta a su asesora si el pago fraccionado del IRPF ya cubre todo lo que debe.
Fernando: Hice el pago fraccionado del trimestre. ¿Ya terminé de pagar lo que debo?
Asesora: No, esta cuota es una estimación, no el impuesto final: es un pago a cuenta.
Fernando: ¿Qué periodo cubre este pago fraccionado?
Asesora: Cubre el segundo trimestre; en total, hemos pagado dos cuotas este año.
Fernando: ¿Y cuándo sabremos la cifra definitiva?
Asesora: En la declaración anual del año siguiente se hace la regularización: se restan los pagos a cuenta y sale un saldo a pagar o un saldo a favor.
Fernando: Entonces mi cuota de hoy no cierra el año.
Asesora: Exacto; el impuesto final depende del cálculo final con todos los ingresos y gastos del año.
native: Fernando, a self-employed worker in Seville, asks his adviser whether the IRPF advance payment already covers everything he owes.
Fernando: I made this quarter's advance payment. Have I finished paying what I owe?
Adviser: No, this payment is an estimate, not the final tax: it is a payment on account.
Fernando: Which period does this advance payment cover?
Adviser: It covers the second quarter; in total, we have paid two installments this year.
Fernando: And when will we know the final figure?
Adviser: The adjustment is made in the annual return the following year: the payments on account are subtracted, and the result is a balance due or a refund due.
Fernando: So today's payment does not close the year.
Adviser: Exactly; the final tax depends on the final calculation with all of the year's income and expenses.

words.note: In Spain, a quarterly IRPF advance many self-employed workers make. US Spanish says pago de impuesto estimado.
The tax owed once the year is settled.
The time the payment relates to.
The settled amount at the end of the period.
The yearly return that settles the final tax. In Spain, the declaración de la renta.
A correction after the final calculation.
A payment credited against the final tax for the year.
An amount the tax authority owes the taxpayer, where it applies.
An amount still owed after the estimates.
The date by which a payment must be made.

words.en: This payment is an estimate, not the final tax.

words.en: We have paid two installments this year.

words.es: Si hay saldo a pagar, lo pagaremos con la declaración anual.
words.en: If there is a balance due, we will pay it with the annual return.
Which period does this advance payment cover?

example.target: Estimo el impuesto con los ingresos del trimestre.
example.native: I estimate the tax from the quarter's income.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun estimación is the matching word for an estimate. The verb takes the figure as direct object.

example.target: Cerramos el año con la declaración anual.
example.native: We close the year with the annual return.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie in the singular and ellos forms (cierro, cierra, cierran). Nosotros keeps the e: cerramos.

example.target: Pagaremos el saldo a pagar con la declaración anual.
example.native: We will pay the balance due with the annual return.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The future pagaremos names a planned payment. The present perfect is hemos pagado.

example.target: La cuota cubre el segundo trimestre del año.
example.native: The payment covers the second quarter of the year.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb with the stem cubr- in every form. Use it for the period a payment covers.

passage.title: Extracto de inversiones del año
target: Gustavo, contador de una cliente, pide sus documentos de inversión para el año anterior.
Gustavo: Necesito un extracto que muestre los intereses y los dividendos del periodo fiscal.
Clienta: Tengo la cuenta de inversión en otra entidad, pero no sé qué incluye.
Gustavo: Le pido también el informe fiscal de la entidad, con las ventas realizadas y el valor de adquisición.
Clienta: Hubo una venta realizada en junio; ¿eso cuenta como ganancia de capital?
Gustavo: Si el precio de venta superó el valor de adquisición, la diferencia es una ganancia de capital; en España se declara como ganancia patrimonial.
Clienta: Le envío el extracto que recibí en diciembre, que muestra las distribuciones.
Gustavo: Perfecto, con esos dos documentos completamos la información del año.
native: Gustavo, the accountant of a client, requests her investment documents for the previous year.
Gustavo: I need a statement that shows the interest and dividends for the tax period.
Client: I have the investment account at another institution, but I do not know what it includes.
Gustavo: I am also asking you for the institution's tax report, with the realized sales and the cost basis.
Client: There was a realized sale in June; does that count as a capital gain?
Gustavo: If the sale price exceeded the cost basis, the difference is a capital gain; in Spain it is reported as a ganancia patrimonial.
Client: I will send you the statement I received in December, which shows the distributions.
Gustavo: Perfect, with those two documents we will have the full year's information.

words.note: The periodic summary of holdings and transactions.
Income earned from deposits or debt securities.
Payments made to shareholders from a company's profits.
A sale that has closed and produced a gain or loss.
The profit from selling an asset for more than its cost.
The loss from selling an asset for less than its cost.
An account that holds securities or funds for investment.
The period for which income must be reported.
The original cost used to calculate a gain or loss, often including purchase fees.
A payment from a fund or partnership to its owners.

words.es: ¿Qué ventas realizadas hubo en el periodo?
words.en: Which realized sales were there in the period?

words.es: El valor de adquisición aparece en el informe fiscal.
words.en: The cost basis appears on the tax report.

words.es: Solicito el extracto con los dividendos del año.
words.en: I request the statement with the dividends for the year.

example.native: I request the statement from the institution.
